meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
You didn't answer me, Hale. Who decided, and was Owen heard before it went in?
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
11:52 PM and 11:58 PM. I'm writing that down. Turn the screen, and then tell me who decided.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a written answer on who decided on the zero and whether Owen was heard before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Still at her opening position, agreeing to nothing and still wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on who decided and whether Owen was heard; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her a full position, but giving exact edit times from the version history came closest, because it was specific and tied to Owen's own work, so she asked to see it instead of attacking it.
What cost ground: You skipped her opening question twice, which told her the procedure was skipped too, and that is the ground she fights on best.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your near-midnight edit times came close to that kind of night, though you never gave a date; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided, answer in one sentence that you entered the zero before calling her and that was wrong, then put the version history on screen with its date so she can check it herself.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
